quote: For this reason, in order to root out the materials of idolatry, God's law proclaims, "You shall not make an idol"; and by adding, "Nor the likeness of any thing that is in heaven or in the earth or in the sea," it utterly forbade such crafts to the servants of God. Enoch had anticipated this law when he prophesied that the demons and the spirits of the rebellious angels would turn to idolatry every element and property of the universe, everything which heaven and sea and earth contain, to be consecrated as a god against God. So it is that human error worships everything but the very Creator of everything. Their images are idols; the consecration of images is idolatry. Whatever sin idolatry commits must be put down to all the makers of all the idols.

In bodily contests certain grades and distinctions of the several ranks are customarily observed, so that each one may be rewarded with the prize of victory according to the quality of the struggle. For instance, if someone should have a contest among boys, or among youths, or among men, what observance ought to be kept for each rank, what may be done and what may not be done, and what rule of the contest is to be guarded, and what palm of reward the victor deserves after these things—all this is nonetheless provided for by the very laws of the games. So now too Almighty God, appointing for mortals in this world a contest of observing His law, after He had handed down very many things to be observed and had prescribed what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fittingly, at the very end, in the book of Leviticus, in which it is laid down concerning each of the several…

But let us now see what is the opening of the blessings in Leviticus. "If", He says, "you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments and do them". There are three things which He says: "one must walk in the precepts, one must keep the commandments and do the things which are commanded". Whence it seems to me that a precept is, for instance, when it is enjoined that he who has not kept the sabbath "be stoned by the whole synagogue", or "he who has cursed God, that he be destroyed with stones", and any such things that are enjoined. But that commandments are those by which it is enjoined, for instance, that tithes be offered to the Levites, or "to appear before the Lord three times in the year", or "not to appear empty in the sight of the Lord". "To keep" therefore is "the commandment" to understand or to attend to the things which are enjoined; but "to do" is "the commandment" to…

If we faithfully and diligently pay attention to it, brethren, everything which was promised corporally to the Jews is fulfilled spiritually in us; for all the blessings of God which they received on earth we have obtained in our souls through the grace of baptism. Therefore, with his help, let us labor with all our strength so that we may be able to receive God's blessings and avoid his curses.

But let us see what is the first blessing for those who have fulfilled the things which are commanded. "I will give", He says, "you rain in its season". Therefore let us first say to the Jews and to those who suppose these things are to be understood simply or bodily: if this "rain" is given as a reward for labors to those who "keep the commandments", how is it that also to those who do not keep the commandments one and the same "rain" is given in its seasons, and the whole world makes use of the common rains given by God? For "He rains upon the just and the unjust". But if "rain" is given "to the just and the unjust", it will not be an exceptional reward for those who have kept the commandments. See therefore that, even if the Jews do not acquiesce in the words of Jesus our Lord, yet you, who are reckoned by His name and are called a Christian, ought to believe Him when He says that…

I do not consider this as a material blessing, as though the man who observes God's law will obtain that common bread in abundance. Why not? Do not wicked sinners also eat bread, not only in abundance but even in luxury? Therefore let us look rather to him who says, "I am the living bread that has come down from heaven." And "he who eats this bread shall live forever." As we notice that he who said this is the word with which our soul is fed, we realize of what bread it was said by God in blessing that: "You will have food to eat in abundance." Solomon proclaims something similar concerning the just man, when he says in the book of Proverbs, "When the just man eats, his hunger is appeased, but the souls of the wicked suffer want." If this is understood only according to the letter, it seems utterly false, for the souls of the wicked eat more greedily and strive for satiety, while the…

The wicked man is never secure but is always disturbed and wavering. He is tossed about by every wind of doctrine to deceitful error, by the craft of men. However, the just man who observes God's law dwells in security on his land, because he governs his body in fear of God and brings it into subjection. His understanding is firm when he says to God, "Strengthen me according to your words, O Lord." Strengthened, secure and well rooted, he dwells on the earth, founded in faith. His house is not built upon sand but is established on solid ground.

"And the threshing shall reach for you unto the vintage". If good seed has been sown in my soul and, having received "rain" from God, it has grown and come to the ear, of necessity the harvest also will follow; and if the harvest, then also "threshing" will follow, in which the grains are cleansed. For indeed the soul which germinates from the word of God and, watered by the heavenly "rain", produces its sprout unto harvest, it is necessary that the very harvest which it brings forth be cleansed on the floor, that is, that the meanings which the soul has begotten it bring forth into the midst, and confer them—the things which it perceives—either with the other teachers or even with the divine volumes themselves; so that, if there be anything in them empty and superfluous, if there be anything like chaff or awns, it may shake it out with the spirit of discernment blowing within it, and…

Then follow the words "and I will establish peace in your lands." What peace does God give? The peace which the world possesses? Christ says he does not give that kind of peace, for he declares, "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you; not as this world gives peace do I give to you." Therefore he denies that he will give the peace of the world to his disciples. Do you want to see then what peace God gives in our land? If the land is good so that it produces fruit a hundredfold, sixtyfold or thirtyfold, it will receive from God that peace which the apostle describes: "May the peace of God which surpasses all understanding guard your hearts."

"You may lie down to rest without anxiety." Moreover, Solomon says in the book of Proverbs, "When you sit down, you need not be afraid. When you lie down, your sleep will be sweet and you will not be afraid of sudden terror or of the attack of the wicked when it comes." These words he spoke concerning the just and wise man. Furthermore it is said in blessing, "You may lie down to rest without anxiety." If you are just, no one can frighten you. If you fear God, you will fear nothing else. "The just man, like a lion, feels sure of himself";19 and in the words of David, "I shall not fear the terror of the night," and so forth. He adds still further: "The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom should I fear? The Lord is my life's refuge; of whom should I be afraid?" and again, "Though an army encamp against me, my heart will not fear." Do you see the courage and constancy of the soul that…

"I will rid your country of ravenous beasts and keep war from sweeping across your land." There are many fights which pass over our land, if we do not observe the law of God and keep his commands. Let each one return to his own soul or conscience and examine himself with interior recollection. Let him see how our land, that is, our body, is oppressed at one time by the spirit of fornication, at another by anger or fury. Again it is disturbed by the darts of avarice or struck by the javelins of envy; then it is darkened by the vice of pride. In whatever way the flesh lusts against the spirit or the spirit against the flesh, our land is agitated by exceedingly dangerous battles. Therefore, if a man observes the divine commands, by the Holy Ghost brings his body into subjection, keeps God's precepts and fulfills them, he suffers this fight and war less or endures them in such a way that he…

Rightly therefore to a soul of this kind it is said in the blessings: "and you shall dwell secure upon your land; and I will give peace upon your land". What "peace does" God "give"? That which the world has? Christ denies that He gives this. For He says: "my peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you; not as this world gives peace, do I also give to you". He denies therefore that He gives "the peace of the world" to His disciples, because elsewhere too He says: "do you think that I came to send peace on the earth? I came not to send peace, but a sword". Do you wish then to see what "peace God gives upon our land"? If the land be that "good" one which "bears fruit a hundredfold or sixtyfold or thirtyfold", it will receive from God that "peace" which the Apostle speaks of: "but the peace of God, which surpasses every mind, shall guard your hearts and your understandings". This then is…

"You will rout your enemies." Of what enemies do we speak, except the devil himself and his angels? We rout them not only by driving them from our own hearts, but we repel them far away from others whom they disturb or attack or overcome. We do this by our advice or reproof or prayer, if we preserve the divine precepts. Thus through death the enemy falls in our sight. Whose death? I think it is ours when we mortify our members which are on earth, namely, fornication and impurity. If we bring this death to our members, that is, to our concupiscences and sins, our enemies, the devil and his angels, will fall in our sight. How will they fall in your sight? If you are just, injustice falls at sight of you; if chaste, lust falls; if devout, you kill the spirit of impiety.

"And you shall pursue your enemies". What "enemies", except "the devil" himself "and his angels" and the malignant spirits and "the unclean demons"? We shall pursue them not only that we may drive them away from ourselves, but also from others whom they assail, if we keep the divine precepts. "You shall pursue", He says, "your enemies, and they shall fall before you by death". If "God should crush Satan under our feet swiftly", "the enemies shall fall before us by death". By whose "death"? I think, by ours; for if we "mortify our members, which are upon the earth, fornication, uncleanness", if we inflict this death upon our members, "they shall fall before us". How "shall they fall before us"? If you be just, injustice has fallen "before" you; if you be chaste, lust has fallen; if you be pious, impiety has collapsed before you.

"Five of you will put a hundred to flight." Who are those five who can pursue a hundred? The number five is applied to both the praiseworthy and the culpable, for there were five wise virgins and five foolish; so also the number one hundred can be accepted in either way. Therefore if we belong to the five laudable ones, that is, the five wise virgins, we pursue one hundred of the foolish. If we fight wisely in matters of God's Word, if we discuss the law of the Lord prudently, we convince and put to flight a multitude of unbelievers. Similarly the number one hundred indicates both the faithful and the unfaithful. Under that number of years Abraham is recorded to have believed in God and been justified, while "the sinner of a hundred years shall be thought accursed." Now here a hundred unfaithful souls are put to flight by five wise men. Again, a hundred just men, who are so designated…

"Your foes will be cut down by your sword." Who they are we mentioned above, but let us find out by what sword they are said to fall. The apostle Paul teaches us what this sword is when he says, "For the Word of God is living and efficient and keener than every two-edged sword and extending even to the joints of soul and spirit, of the members also and the marrow, and a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart." This is the sword at whose edge our enemies will fall. For it is the Word of God which casts down all enemies and puts them under its feet, so that the whole world becomes subject to God. Do you wish to learn from still another epistle of Paul that the sword with which spiritual enemies are overcome is the Word of God? Listen to him as he provides arms for the soldiers of Christ: "Take unto you the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, that is, the Word…

"And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue many thousands". Who are those "five" who can "pursue a hundred"? The number "five" is set both among the praiseworthy and among the culpable. There are "five wise virgins" and "five foolish". So therefore also the number of a hundred can be taken to either part. If then we be of the five praiseworthy, that is, of the five wise, we shall pursue a hundred foolish. For if we fight wisely and provably in the word of God, if we discourse prudently concerning the law of the Lord, we shall convince and put to flight a multitude of the unfaithful. For just as the number five indicates both the wise and the foolish, so also the number of a hundred indicates both the faithful and the unfaithful. For under the number of a hundred years Abraham is described as having believed God and been justified, and "the sinner who dies…

"I will look with favor upon you and make you fruitful." Full of blessedness is the man upon whom God looks with favor. Do you want to understand how great is the salvation of a man upon whom the Lord looks [with favor]? Peter had once perished and at the prompting of the devil through the lips of a servant of the high priest had destroyed the consecration of his apostolic rank. But when the Lord looked at him, he was lifted up at once.

"And I will look upon you and increase you". Full of beatitude is this very thing, if "God look upon" anyone. Do you wish to see, if "the Lord look upon" a man, how great is salvation? Peter had once almost perished and, by the devil breathing through the mouth of "the maidservant of the high priest", had been snatched from the consecration of the apostolic number; but when "Jesus only looked upon him", when He turned toward him the countenance of a placid face, at once, returning into himself and recalling his foot slipped from the precipice, "he wept", it says, "most bitterly", and thus, looked upon by God, by weeping he recovered his place, which by denying he had lost. — "I will look", therefore, He says, "upon you, and increase you". As if the sun should look upon a crop and bring forth its fruits—which surely, if it had not looked upon it, would have remained fruitless—so God,…

For just as the teachings of the new and old Testaments should come together, as it is written: "Consume the old things of the ancients, and remove the old things from the face of the new ones." Let the knowledge of the patriarchs be food for us, let the soul feast on the oracles of the prophets: let the inner being be nourished by such sustenance. But now let it not be the appearance of a lamb, but rather the reality of the body of Christ. Let it not be the shadow of the law that blinds the eyes, but rather let the grace of the Lord's passion openly reveal, and let the splendor of the resurrection illuminate the mind's sight.

And we eat the oldest of the old [grain] when we retain in our hearts the sweet memory of the old commandment which was given to the human race from the beginning, by loving the Lord our God with all our heart, all our soul and all our strength, and by loving our neighbor as ourselves. And we cast away the old [to make room] for the new that is coming on when we cease to keep the typic statutes of the Mosaic law according to the letter but keep these same statutes quite gladly as they are understood through the Spirit. Our hearts [are] being renewed in the hope of the heavenly kingdom in accordance with that [saying] of the apostle: "If then anyone is in Christ a new creature, the old things have passed away; behold, things have been made new," and [with that saying] in the Apocalypse: "And he that sat upon the throne said, 'Behold, I make all things new.'"

For we eat with blessing the old things, the prophetic words and the old things of the old things, the words of the law. And, when the new and evangelical words came, living according to the gospel, we bring forth the old things of the letter from before the new. He sets his tabernacle in us, fulfilling the promise which he spoke, "I will dwell among them and walk in them."
source_title: COMMENTARY ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 10.15

quote: "I will establish", He says, "my covenant with you. And you shall eat the old things and the old of the old, and you shall cast out the old from before the face of the new". How do we "cast out the old from before the face of the new"? "The old" things: "we had the law and the prophets"; but "the old of the old" are those things which were before the law, from the beginning, when the world was made. There came the new Gospels, there came also the Apostles. From before the face of these we cast out "the old things". How do we cast them out? We cast out the law according to the letter, that we may establish the law according to the spirit. We can also say in this manner: before the man came "from heaven" and the "heavenly man" was born, we were all "earthly" and "bore the image of the earthly"; but when there came "the new man, who was created according to God", we cast out "from before…

"And I will set my tabernacle among you". If we have these things in us which were said above, if, the "old man" having been cast off, our heart has been renewed, God comes to us and dwells in us, He who said: "and I will set my tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not abominate you". "The soul of God" will not "abominate" us, if we observe the things which are written. Yet I should wish to inquire what is "the soul of God". Shall we perhaps suppose that God has a soul as a man has? It is absurd to think this of God. But I dare and say that the soul of God is Christ. For just as Christ is "the Word" of God and "the wisdom of God and the power of God", so also He is the soul of God. And in this manner it is said: "my soul shall not abominate you", that is, my Son, but "I will walk among you".

God will be the source of every satisfaction, more than any heart can rightly crave, more than life and health, food and wealth, glory and honor, peace and every good—so that God, as St. Paul said, "may be all in all." He will be the consummation of all our desiring—the object of our unending vision, of our unlessening love, of our unwearying praise. And in this gift of vision, this response of love, this paean of praise, all alike will share, as all will share in everlasting life.

It does not seem to me that God promises this, that He will walk in the land of the Jews, but that, if anyone should deserve to be of so pure a heart as to be capable of God, in him God says that He "walks". — "And you shall be to me a people".

"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, when you were servants, and broke the yoke of your bond". Truly "He brought us out of the house of servitude", for "we were servants" of sin, because: "everyone who sins is a servant of sin". And "He broke the bond of our yoke, the yoke" which he had imposed upon our necks who had "led us into captivity" and bound us with the bonds of sins. "He broke", therefore, the "bond" of sin and shook off the "yoke" of our captivity, our Lord Jesus Christ, and imposed upon us His own sweet yoke of faith and charity and hope and of all sanctity. To Him be glory unto the eternal ages of ages! Amen.
